questions.question: At what PGR dose did regression estimate maximal germination, regardless of seed type?
questions.rationale: The germination response was quadratic, with the estimated maximum at 10.3 mL/kg.
questions.evidence_quote: There was a quadratic effect of growth regulator levels on germination regardless of seed type. According to the equation estimated by regression, the treatment of seeds with 10.3 mL.kg -1 promotes greater germination.

questions.question: Which PGR dose was estimated to maximize root dry mass, and how does it compare with the germination optimum?

options.A: 12.8 mL/kg, higher than the 10.3 mL/kg germination optimum.
options.B: 10.3 mL/kg, higher than the 8.85 mL/kg germination optimum.
options.C: 8.85 mL/kg, lower than the 12.8 mL/kg germination optimum.
options.D: 24 mL/kg, equal to the germination optimum.

questions.rationale: The response optima differed by outcome: root dry mass peaked at a higher estimated dose than germination.
questions.evidence_quote: Based on the estimated equation, the treatment of Brachiaria decumbens cv. Basilisk seeds with 12.8 mL.kg -1 of growth regulator resulted in higher root dry mass production (Table 3 ).

questions.question: For coated seeds, at what PGR levels were the reported leaf and pseudostem dry-mass optima?
questions.rationale: The paper gives separate estimated optima for leaf and pseudostem mass in coated seeds.
questions.evidence_quote: In the absence of treatment or at the lowest level tested (8.0 mL.kg -1 ), higher production of leaf and pseudostem dry mass was observed for coated seeds, corresponding to the treatment using 8.85 and 9.57 mL.kg -1 , respectively.

questions.question: What PGR levels maximized leaf and pseudostem dry-mass production for conventional seeds?
questions.rationale: Conventional seed required higher estimated PGR doses than coated seed for these two structures.
questions.evidence_quote: Conventional seeds required higher levels of the treatment for leaf and pseudostem dry mass production, being 15.5 and 18.1 mL.kg -1 , respectively (Table 4 ).

questions.question: Which design was used to assess seed type and PGR dose in the first experiment?

options.A: A completely randomized 2×4 factorial: two seed types and four PGR levels.
options.B: A randomized-block 2×3 factorial: two seed types and three PGR levels.
options.C: A 4×4 factorial with four seed types and four PGR levels.
options.D: A completely randomized 2×4 split-plot with four nitrogen regimes only.

questions.rationale: Experiment 1 crossed coated/conventional seed with four PGR doses in a completely randomized design.
questions.evidence_quote:
A 2 x 4 factorial scheme was used in a completely randomized design (CRD).
Two commercial seed types (coated and conventional) and four levels of the growth regulator (0, 8, 16, 24 mL.kg -1 of seed) were used according to the manufacturer's recommendation.

questions.question: What was the PGR formulation applied to seeds?
questions.rationale: The mixture contained the stated concentrations of three hormone classes, which matters when interpreting the observed response as a combined formulation.
questions.evidence_quote: The PGR was composed of auxin (0.05 mg.L -1 ), cytokinin (0.09 mg.L -1 ) and gibberellin (0.05 mg.L -1 ).

questions.question: How many days after sowing were germination counts conducted, and what two metrics were derived?

options.A: Daily for 14 days, for germination percentage and germination speed index.
options.B: Daily for 30 days, for biomass and root volume.
options.C: Every 6 hours for 48 hours, for mortality and viability.
options.D: At 30 days only, for chlorophyll and carotenoids.

questions.rationale: The study tracked daily emergence over a 14-day window and calculated both final germination and speed index.
questions.evidence_quote: Daily counts of germinated seeds were carried out for 14 days to determine germination percentage and germination speed index (GSI)

questions.question: How did PGR interact with nitrogen fertilization for leaf, stem, shoot, and root dry mass?

options.A: The interaction was significant; soil fertilization generally gave high yields, while PGR combined with multiple soil+foliar fertilization reduced leaf, stem, and shoot production relative to no PGR.
options.B: The interaction was nonsignificant and PGR increased all structures under every fertilization method.
options.C: Only root mass showed an interaction; foliar N alone maximized all structures.
options.D: PGR reduced all biomass regardless of N treatment.

questions.rationale: Effects depended on the combination: soil N was generally favorable, but multiple fertilization combined with PGR did not yield additive gains for aboveground structures.
questions.evidence_quote: The interaction between the use of PGR and nitrogen fertilization methods was significant for dry mass production of leaf, stem, shoot, and root. Dry mass production of stem, leaf, and shoot was greater when the use of PGR and soil fertilization were combined, although soil fertilization resulted in higher yields for the evaluated structures regardless of PGR. The use of PGR reduced leaf, stem, and shoot production when combined with multiple fertilization (soil + foliar), differing from the absence of PGR, which was similar to soil fertilization when submitted to multiple fertilization.

questions.question: What was the effect of PGR on root dry mass under the different N treatments?

options.A: PGR increased root dry mass only with multiple fertilization; it had no influence under other fertilization types.
options.B: PGR increased root dry mass only with soil fertilization.
options.C: PGR decreased root mass under multiple fertilization and increased it under all others.
options.D: PGR had no effect on root mass in any treatment.

questions.rationale: The interaction for root mass was specific: a PGR benefit appeared with combined soil-plus-foliar fertilization only.
questions.evidence_quote: The use of PGR increased root dry mass production only when combined with multiple fertilization; for the other fertilization types, no influence of growth regulators was observed

questions.question: Which nitrogen-fertilization conclusion is supported, and what limitation should be kept in mind?

options.A: Soil N promoted greater biomass and root volume, while foliar N alone showed no general yield influence; the findings are greenhouse/pot-based.
options.B: Foliar N alone maximized all biomass, validated in multi-year field trials.
options.C: Nitrogen had no effect on any plant structure.
options.D: Only foliar N was studied, so soil comparisons are unavailable.

questions.rationale: The abstract/conclusion favors soil fertilization for yield, while the methods describe greenhouse pots and short experimental windows rather than field-scale confirmation.
questions.evidence_quote: Soil N-fertilization resulted in higher dry mass productions of leaf, stem, shoot and root, as well as for root volume.
